answer: In an agent marketplace trading timber, each identity must lock a $100 bond for 30 days before it can submit bids, and each bond grants the same capped bidding capacity. Registration opens at dawn, with each bond recorded in a public audit thread. Creating aliases therefore adds no free capacity: an attacker running 1,000 eligible identities must immobilize $100,000 for a month, paying financing costs on every fake account.
